The patient, aged 45, comes to the consultation presenting nail alterations, malformations in the epiphysis of the third toe, diffuse mesangial fibrosis, ureteral malformation, episodes of angina pectoris and enlargement of the epiphysis of the distal phalanx of the third toe.


The patient reports a history of high blood pressure and type 2 diabetes.


The physical examination reveals the presence of split nails, alterations in the epiphysis of the third toe, diffuse mesangial fibrosis and enlargement of the epiphysis of the distal phalanx of the third toe.


After evaluating the symptoms and findings in the physical examination, the diagnosis of Alport Syndrome is established, a genetic disease that mainly affects the kidneys, ears and eyes.


Symptomatic treatment for angina pectoris is indicated, as well as control of arterial hypertension and follow-up by nephrology for the management of kidney disease.

The patient is given the instructions and a follow-up consultation is scheduled in one month.

A 35-year-old patient, , comes to the clinic with a history of pregestational diabetes. She reports a triangular-shaped deformity in the intermediate phalanges of the hand, a delay in social evolution, and a lack of development of the antihelix. In addition, she has recently been diagnosed with ureteral stenosis and a kidney tumor has been identified in previous imaging studies.



On examination, the deformity in the intermediate phalanges of the hand described by the patient is observed, as well as the lack of development of the antihelix in both earlobes. No other relevant findings are seen in the physical examination.



1. Deformity in the intermediate phalanges of the hand.
2. Lack of development of the antihelix.
3. Ureteral stenosis.
4. Kidney tumor.
5. Delay in social evolution.

Treatment plan

Additional studies will be performed to assess the extent and characteristics of the kidney tumor. Likewise, the need for surgical intervention to correct the ureteral stenosis will be assessed. Follow-up with the social work service will be recommended to address the delay in social evolution.

A detailed report will be issued to your primary care physician.

Patient Davide Pellegrini
 The patient, 45 years old, comes to the consultation due to alteration of the renal functional unit, leukocytosis, progressive sensory neuropathy, antithrombin III deficiency, hypoplastic ureter, congenital nephropathy with proteinuria, constriction of the middle part of the nose and fan-shaped ear. These symptoms have been progressing in recent weeks, causing general discomfort in the patient.

 The patient has no relevant medical history, no history of kidney disease in the family.

 On examination, edema in the lower limbs, skin pallor, decreased sensitivity in the extremities, as well as a marked constriction in the middle part of the nose and an abnormal shape in the ear are observed.

 A possible chronic kidney disease is suspected, associated with a genetic alteration that affects multiple systems of the patient, including the peripheral nervous system and the vascular system. Additional studies are required to confirm the diagnosis.

 Symptomatic treatment is started to control proteinuria and follow-up with a nephrologist and geneticist is scheduled for comprehensive study and management of the case.

This document is issued at the request of the patient to continue the study at another medical center.

The patient, aged 45, comes to the consultation due to paralysis of the ocular muscles, action tremor and visual deficit of genetic origin. In addition, the presence of benign cortical renal neoplasia and ureterohydronephrosis has been observed in previous studies.


The patient reports a history of recurrent staphylococcal infections, lack of permanent molar and osteogenesis imperfecta of the ear.


On physical examination, paralysis of the ocular muscles, action tremor and visual deficit are evident. A renal mass is palpated and ureterohydronephrosis is confirmed in imaging tests.


The diagnosis of Gorlin-Goltz syndrome is proposed, a rare genetic disease characterized by the presence of benign skin neoplasms, bone defects, ocular disorders and predisposition to renal tumors.


Multidisciplinary treatment will be initiated with follow-up by ophthalmology, neurology, urology and genetics. Periodic check-ups will be performed to monitor the evolution of the renal and ocular lesions.

The patient, 45 years old, comes to the consultation presenting uneven bone thickening in the distal phalanx of the third finger of the right hand, deterioration of the spinocerebellar pathway, alteration of the brainstem bridge, repetitive infections by Serratia marcescens, bifurcated ureter, tubulointerstitial irregularity and visual alteration in the cerebral cortex.


The patient reports previous episodes of recurrent infections, as well as progressive vision problems in recent months. He does not report any recent history of trauma.


On examination, bone thickening is observed in the distal phalanx of the third finger of the right hand, as well as signs of involvement of the spinocerebellar pathway and the brain stem bridge. The presence of a bifurcated ureter is also evident in imaging studies, along with findings of tubulointerstitial irregularity.


Given the symptoms presented, the possibility of a genetically based pathological process affecting multiple systems is raised, including the bone, neurological, renal and visual systems. Additional study is required to determine the origin and adequate management of the identified alterations.


Additional tests will be performed for an accurate diagnosis, as well as symptomatic treatment will be established to address the present clinical manifestations.

A follow-up appointment is made for monitoring and evolution of the findings.

Symptomatic treatment for bladder infections will be started and follow-up will be scheduled with the Genetics service for genetic study and counseling.

The patient has no relevant medical history. She does not smoke and consumes alcohol occasionally.


A deformity is observed in the upper incisor, as well as an abnormal epiphysis in the first metacarpal. The rest of the physical examination was within normal parameters.

Studies Performed
Urinalysis has been performed which confirmed the presence of intermediate grade proteinuria. Genetic studies have also been performed which have revealed the presence of hyperoxanthinuria.

Recommended 
- Control of proteinuria
- Dental treatment to correct the incisor deformity
- Follow-up with a geneticist to manage hyperoxanthinuria

The patient is scheduled for a check-up in one month.

The patient, 45 years old, comes to the consultation due to a series of symptoms that have been appearing progressively in recent months.

Personal history
The patient does not report any relevant medical history, except for an episode of fracture in the bones of the forearm 2 years ago, which was treated conservatively.


After the clinical evaluation, several significant findings have been identified. The patient presents Leber's optic neuropathy, malformation of the epididymis, neurological dysfunction, osteoarthritis of the distal interphalangeal joint, papillary renal carcinoma and mandibular hypoplasia.


A genetic disorder affecting multiple body systems is suspected, which would explain the variety of symptoms present in the patient. Genetic studies are required to confirm the diagnosis.

Management plan
Specific genetic tests will be performed to identify the mutation responsible for the symptoms present in the patient. A consultation with the genetics service will also be arranged for advice and follow-up.

Next appointment
The patient is scheduled for a review of results and follow-up planning within a period of 4 weeks.

The patient, 45 years old, comes to the consultation due to a series of symptoms that have been progressing in recent weeks. The main symptoms include the presence of a winged scapula, static blindness, recurrent splenic enlargement, anomaly in the growth zones of the elbow, hypoplastic bladder, and spasticity.


The patient does not report any relevant medical history. He has no known allergies.


The presence of a winged scapula is clearly observed in the physical examination, as well as static blindness and spasticity in the lower limbs. Splenic enlargement is palpated and anomaly is evident in the growth zones of the elbow. In addition, the presence of a hypoplastic bladder is noted in the examination.


Based on the symptoms presented by the patient, a possible neurometabolic syndrome is suspected. Additional studies are required to confirm the diagnosis.

Management plan
Imaging tests (magnetic resonance imaging, ultrasound) and laboratory tests (blood count, metabolic profile) will be requested to complete the diagnostic study. The patient will be referred to genetics and neurology specialists for a multidisciplinary approach.

A follow-up appointment is scheduled in one month to review the results and follow up on the case.

Patient Angelo Mancini
 The patient, 45 years old, comes to the consultation due to chronic lower back pain, difficulty walking due to weakness in the legs and alterations in urination. In addition, a deformity is observed in the lumbar and gluteal region.

 On examination, an incomplete version of the buttocks, nodular goiter on palpation, hypoplasia of the sella turcica and signs of radicular compression are evident. In addition, a malignant peripheral nerve tumor is detected in the lumbar region.

Complementary studies A lumbar magnetic resonance is performed, which confirms the diagnosis of spondylolysis with spondylolisthesis, as well as the presence of a peripheral nerve tumor. In addition, hypoplasia of the sella turcica is observed on brain resonance.

 Based on clinical and radiological findings, a diagnosis of spondylolysis with spondylolisthesis, malignant peripheral nerve tumor, nodular goiter, hypoplasia of the sella turcica, and urinary retention secondary to radicular compression is established.

 Surgical treatment is indicated for the correction of spondylolisthesis and resection of the peripheral nerve tumor. Hormonal therapy is also prescribed for nodular goiter and the need for treatment for urinary retention is evaluated.

Follow-up The patient is monitored by the Neurosurgery and Endocrinology service for progressive monitoring and comprehensive management of his pathology.

These include the presence of an anterior sacral meningocele, flaccid skin in various areas of the body, frontal muscle dysfunction, knotted net retinopathy, urethral atresia in the case of women, gradual drooping of the upper eyelid, and asymmetric epiphysis of the distal phalanx of the second finger of the hand.

Personal history
The patient does not report any relevant medical history or previous surgeries.


On physical examination, the presence of the symptoms mentioned above is observed. The presence of an anterior sacral meningocele is evident, as well as flaccid skin and dysfunction of the frontal muscle. The ophthalmological examination confirms retinopathy in the form of a knotted network. Likewise, urethral atresia is confirmed in the patient, as well as the gradual drooping of the upper eyelid and the asymmetrical epiphysis of the distal phalanx of the second finger of the hand.


A possible rare genetic syndrome affecting multiple body systems is suspected, which would explain the presence of the various symptoms observed in the patient. Genetic studies are required to confirm the diagnosis.


The patient will be referred to a genetics consultation for specific diagnostic tests and to establish an appropriate follow-up and treatment plan.

 The patient, a 45-year-old woman, comes to the doctor's office presenting muscle weakness in the legs, difficulty walking, pain and inflammation in the tongue, alterations in the skin of the palms of the hands, decreased oligodendrocytes, damage to the renal glomeruli, and peripheral neuropathy.

 After a thorough physical examination, weakness in the peroneal muscles, inflammation of the tongue, altered palmar dermatoglyphics, and signs of peripheral neuropathy are observed. Laboratory tests reveal a decrease in oligodendrocytes and the presence of glomerular nephritis.

 Based on the symptoms presented and the clinical and laboratory findings, the diagnosis of Polymyositis is established, an autoimmune disease that affects skeletal muscles, skin and other organs. Additional studies will be carried out to confirm the diagnosis and establish an appropriate treatment plan.

 Treatment with corticosteroids is started and physiotherapy is indicated to improve the patient's muscle strength and mobility.

Follow-up The patient must attend periodic check-ups to evaluate the response to treatment and make the necessary adjustments.

The patient, aged 45, comes to the consultation presenting a complex clinical picture. He reports neurological symptoms such as muscle weakness, alterations in sensitivity and difficulty controlling the bladder. In addition, the presence of vesicles in the oral mucosa is observed, as well as disorders in speech articulation. The patient has also recently experienced episodes of diabetic ketoacidosis. The presence of a hormone-producing adrenal tumor is suspected, which could be related to the symptoms presented. Likewise, a malformation in the mastoid has been identified that could be contributing to the patient's balance and hearing problems.

Tests performed
Nerve conduction studies have been performed that suggest the presence of chronic inflammatory demyelinating polyneuropathy. Imaging tests have also been carried out which have revealed the existence of a tumor in the adrenal gland.


1. Chronic inflammatory demyelinating polyneuropathy
2. Neurogenic bladder
3. Hormone-producing adrenal tumor
4. Diabetic ketoacidosis
5. Mastoid malformation
6. Speech articulation disorders
7. Vesicles in the oral mucosa


A multidisciplinary treatment will be started which will include corticosteroids for polyneuropathy, surgery to remove the adrenal tumor, diabetes control to prevent ketoacidosis, and the need for surgical intervention to correct the mastoid malformation will be evaluated. Measures for the management of neurogenic bladder will be prescribed and follow-up with a speech therapist will be carried out for speech disorders.

Periodic check-ups are scheduled to evaluate the patient's progress and adjust the treatment as necessary.

The patient, aged 55, comes to the consultation due to a postauricular cutaneous fistula, mixed dyslipidemia, cardiac tumor, sleep apnea-hypopnea syndrome, abdominal aortic stenosis, vertebral osteophytes and a ureteral blockage.


The patient has a history of high blood pressure, type 2 diabetes and obesity.


The presence of a postauricular cutaneous fistula with purulent discharge is observed. In addition, the presence of vertebral osteophytes is evident on the spinal X-ray.

Complementary studies
Blood tests were performed that confirmed the presence of mixed dyslipidemia. Echocardiography revealed the presence of a cardiac tumor. Polysomnography showed a high rate of apneas and hypopneas per hour, consistent with sleep apnea-hypopnea syndrome. Abdominal ultrasound revealed abdominal aortic stenosis. Finally, CT showed ureteral obstruction.


1. Postauricular cutaneous fistula
2. Mixed dyslipidemia
3. Cardiac tumor
4. Sleep apnea-hypopnea syndrome
5. Abdominal aortic stenosis
6. Vertebral osteophytes
7. Ureteral obstruction


Antibiotic treatment is indicated for the cutaneous fistula, statins for dyslipidemia, evaluation by the cardiology department for the cardiac tumor, CPAP for the sleep apnea-hypopnea syndrome, evaluation by vascular surgery for the abdominal aortic stenosis, physical therapy for the vertebral osteophytes, and placement of a ureteral catheter for the ureteral obstruction.

A follow-up appointment is scheduled in one month to monitor the prescribed treatments.

 The patient, 45 years old, comes to the consultation presenting dental concretion, hypoplastic fovea, tibial pseudoarthrosis and acute nephrotic nephropathy. He reports pain in the tibial area and edema in the lower limbs. Radiological studies and laboratory tests are performed to evaluate his current condition.

Findings On physical examination, the presence of dental concretion in several teeth, hypoplastic fovea in both eyes, bone deformity in the tibial region and edema in the lower limbs is observed. Laboratory tests reveal massive proteinuria and decreased serum albumin.

 After evaluating the symptoms and the results of the studies performed, the diagnosis of Bone-Concrete Nephropathy Syndrome is established, a rare disease that affects the kidneys, bones and teeth. Treatment with immunosuppressants is started and periodic follow-up is indicated to monitor the evolution of the disease.

 Treatment with corticosteroids, calcineurin inhibitors and support measures are prescribed to control proteinuria and prevent complications.

The patient is instructed on the importance of following medical instructions, maintaining a low-salt diet and periodically monitoring blood pressure and kidney function.

Next appointment The patient is scheduled for a review in two weeks to evaluate the response to treatment and make adjustments if necessary.

 The patient, 50 years old, comes to the consultation presenting oppressive chest pain of sudden onset, radiating to the left arm and neck, accompanied by sweating and a feeling of impending death. He also reports pain in the right iliac fossa and a history of recurrent ear infections.

 The patient is observed in an apparent state of anxiety, sweaty, with pale skin and mucosa. Elevated heart rate, decreased systolic blood pressure. On cardiac auscultation, rhythmic heart sounds are appreciated, with the presence of a murmur. On abdominal palpation, pain is found in the right iliac fossa.

Complementary studies An electrocardiogram was performed showing ST segment elevation in precordial leads. In addition, abdominal ultrasound revealed the presence of a preauricular appendix. In the study of renal function, focal segmental sclerosis of the glomeruli was observed.

 Myocardial infarction with involvement of multiple territories, acute preauricular appendicitis, and focal segmental sclerosis nephropathy.

 Hospital admission is indicated for management of acute myocardial infarction, emergency appendectomy, and medical treatment for nephropathy.

Outpatient follow-up is planned to monitor renal and cardiac function.

The patient, 45 years old, comes to the consultation due to a disorder of the anterior segment of the eye, characterized by auricular telangiectasias and abnormalities in the lower premolar.


The patient has a history of polycystic kidney disease, pulmonary valvular malformations and absence of the upper central incisor.


On examination, auricular telangiectasia and anomaly in the lower premolar are observed. An anterior segment disorder of the eye is also evident.

Complementary tests

On examination, a characteristic facial dysmorphism is observed, as well as exstrophy of the cloacal bladder. The ophthalmological evaluation confirms the presence of tapeto-retinal dystrophy. The patient's clinical picture is consistent with Usher syndrome, a rare genetic disease characterized by the association of sensorineural deafness with retinitis pigmentosa and, in some cases, skeletal malformations.

The patient and his family are explained the prognosis of the disease, as well as the importance of a multidisciplinary approach to improve their quality of life.

A multidisciplinary treatment will be initiated to address the different manifestations of Kanzaki Syndrome, including follow-up by Endocrinology, Ophthalmology, Genetics and Urology.

Periodic check-ups are scheduled to monitor the patient's progress and adjust the treatment as necessary.
